title: Jogi Gui Grilled Yellow Croaker
shortDescription: Yellow croaker is lightly salted, dried, and grilled whole until the skin is browned and the thickest flesh reaches 145°F / 63°C.
culturalContext: Jogi-gui is Korean grilled croaker. Fresh versus salted fish, species sold as croaker, preparation, and ceremonial or everyday context vary; exact market naming requires review.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric grill
Fish basket, perforated grill pan, or narrow-spaced grate

ingredients.preparation: scaled, gutted, and gills removed by fishmonger

instructions.heading: Inspect and thaw safely
instructions.action: Inspect the cold fish and package; reject sour, rancid, fishy, or ammonia odors, soft flesh, damaged packaging, or evidence of temperature abuse.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Fish smells mild, flesh is firm, and the product is cold.
instructions.safetyNote: Reject sour, rancid, fishy, or ammonia odors and damaged or temperature-abused packages.

instructions.heading: Clean and dry
instructions.action: Have the fishmonger scale, gut, and remove gills as appropriate; verify the cavity is clean, rinse briefly only if needed, and dry thoroughly.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Cavity and skin are clean and very dry.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep raw seafood and its juices off ready-to-eat foods; wash hands and sanitize tools afterward.

instructions.heading: Salt under refrigeration
instructions.action: Salt both sides lightly, cover, and refrigerate 15 minutes; blot away released moisture and brush with oil.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The skin is dry with a thin oil sheen.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep seafood refrigerated until the grill is ready.

instructions.heading: Prepare the grill
instructions.action: Preheat and oil a fish basket or narrow-spaced grate; establish medium direct heat and an open cooler zone.
instructions.temperature: Medium direct heat with cooler zone
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The surface is hot, clean, and lightly oiled.
instructions.safetyNote: Never use a fuel-burning grill indoors; follow appliance ventilation instructions.

instructions.heading: Grill and verify
instructions.action: Secure in the basket and grill, turning once when the skin releases, until browned and the thickest edible flesh reaches 145°F / 63°C.
instructions.temperature: Medium direct heat with cooler zone
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Skin is browned, flesh is opaque and flakes, and the thickest edible portion reaches 145°F / 63°C.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a clean thermometer and clean tools after the final turn; verify 145°F / 63°C in the thickest edible portion.

instructions.heading: Serve safely
instructions.action: Transfer with clean tools, rest 2 minutes, and serve whole with a clear warning about bones.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The seafood is on a clean platter and served promptly.
instructions.safetyNote: Whole fish contains pin bones and sharp bones; diners must eat carefully and children require close adult supervision.

grillSetup: Use an outdoor grill or approved indoor electric grill with a clean, lightly oiled fish basket or narrow-spaced grate over medium heat and an open cooler zone.
targetInternalTemperature: 145°F / 63°C in the thickest edible portion; visual cues supplement but do not replace thermometer verification.
visualDonenessCues: Skin is browned and releases from the basket
Flesh is opaque and separates easily
foodSafetyNotes: Keep fish at or below 40°F / 4°C and cook within 2 days of purchase or freeze.
Warn diners about pin bones and sharp bones.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains fish; use dedicated clean tools and verify any pre-seasoned product label.

substitutions: Use another whole fish only after retesting thickness, bone pattern, skin behavior, and timing.
ingredientSourcing: Buy properly chilled yellow croaker from a reputable seller and confirm the market species.
Choose firm fish with a mild smell and intact skin.
makeAhead: Have the fish cleaned by a qualified fishmonger; salt only for the stated refrigerated time before grilling.
storage: Refrigerate cooked seafood in a shallow covered container within 2 hours and use within 3 days pending food-safety approval.
reheating: Reheat only the needed portion to 165°F / 74°C until steaming; avoid repeated reheating.
leftovers: Use properly refrigerated leftovers within the approved window; discard table-exposed portions after unsafe holding.
servingSuggestions: Serve hot with rice, soup, and banchan.

faq.question: Can visual flaking replace a thermometer?
faq.answer: No. Flaking is a supporting cue; verify 145°F / 63°C.

faq.question: Is a whole fish boneless?
faq.answer: No. Warn every diner and supervise children closely.

buyingCues: Fish is refrigerated on ice or frozen solid in intact packaging.
Odor is fresh and mild, never sour, rancid, fishy, or ammonia-like.
Whole fish has firm flesh and, when fresh, clear eyes and red gills.
seafoodPreparation.thawing: Thaw overnight in a covered container in the refrigerator. For rapid thawing, seal in a leakproof bag under cold water and cook immediately; never thaw on the counter.
seafoodPreparation.cleaningOrShellPreparation: Have the fishmonger scale, gut, and remove gills as appropriate; verify the cavity is clean and follow any package directions.
seafoodPreparation.drying: Pat every surface thoroughly dry with disposable paper towels; immediately discard towels and sanitize the work area.
seafoodPreparation.scoringOrSkewering: Make two shallow skin slashes on the thickest side without cutting through bones; test cooking must validate whether scoring improves even cooking.
seafoodPreparation.grillSurfacePreparation: Preheat, clean, and lightly oil a fish basket or narrow-spaced grate.
seafoodPreparation.stickingPrevention: Dry the skin thoroughly, oil lightly, and wait for the skin to release before turning.
seafoodPreparation.approximateTime: 14 minutes, subject to product size and grill output; thermometer verification controls.
donenessCues: Skin is browned and releases from the basket
Flesh is opaque and separates easily
crossContactNotes: Use a dedicated board and tools for raw seafood.
Wash hands with soap and water after raw-seafood contact.
Use a clean thermometer, tools, and platter for cooked seafood.
